title: Bitcoin’s Resilience Stands Out as Stocks Face Geopolitical Pressure
transcript_text: I'm struggling a little bit with today's price action, right, where I'm trying to understand is that the reduction or that rotation into some of the app performance of some of the software, or is there something bigger happening here? Welcome back to Market's Outlook from the New York Stock Exchange. As we get this, we've started New York Stock Exchange's Senior Market Analyst, Michael Ranking joins it now to weigh in on what you should be watching. Hey, Michael. I think thanks for having me, and welcome to the New York Stock Exchange. Thank you so much for having me here. I know you are a veteran here, so maybe I'll get you to show me around the floor. Absolutely. One of these days. Let's talk about what investors should be watching this week. I know there are two big narratives we're dealing with right now. We have AI disruption fears and rising geopolitical risk in the Middle East. Talk to me about what's driving investor positioning. Yeah, I mean, right now we've kind of moved to, we've put some of those AI anxiety fears to the back burner further moment with what's going on in Iran, right? We, markets are really just solely functioned on what oil prices are doing at this point. So overnight we had a massive move higher in oil prices as we saw in escalation in Iran over the weekend. The narrative originally was that this was going to be something that was going to, that the conflict would be over reasonably quickly. We're starting to get signs that that may be a little more prolonged. You started to see some Middle East countries start to reduce production. The straight is completely closed. We saw prices move up to the high right around 120 for ice Brent. We backed off overnight as there's been some reports that the G7 might start to tap some strategic reserves. We've seen the oil markets back off a little bit. But equity markets have been kind of under pressure and we finally started to kind of break to the downside for the first time this year. I saw some chatter on social this morning that markets haven't fully priced in a longer term war. Should this continue for longer than most expect, what are your thoughts there? Yeah, I think that's fair, right? The one thing, there's a couple of things to think about from a US investor perspective, right? The rest of the world, particularly Asia, is much more impacted by the rise in energy prices, right? As we've seen, kind of the US become more energy independent. So about 80% of Middle Eastern oil that goes through the straight goes to Asia, right? So the impact is greater elsewhere in the world. What that's done is it's reversing some of the trades that we've seen throughout much of this year. Talk about what has been ongoing, you've seen global markets outperforming US markets throughout much of this year. Last week, you started to see US markets outperform a little bit more, right? We've also seen like when you get into these periods of volatility, you start to see de-risking happening kind of across asset classes and across just investment portfolios, right? And so as volatility moves higher, you start to see positioning come down. That happens on both sides of the portfolio. So you see kind of long positions get cut, but also short positions, right? So last week, you started to see some of those software stocks that have really been under pressure, given that AI anxiety, like those stocks outperformed and started to move higher. And we also, the US markets are very concentrated in kind of that mega-cap tech area, right? And you've started to see some signs of the defensive nature in some of those stocks that we've seen in prior drawdowns. And you started to see kind of a little bit of bounce there. The NYC FanClust Index was actually up 2% last week when the S&P was down to and you saw small mid-cap indices down about twice the amount. Bring that back to crypto markets for me now. If we're looking at crypto and the public markets, we're looking at ETFs, some of the crypto equities. How's what we've talked about so far going to affect folks for watching these? Yeah, I mean, the price action today is particularly interesting. We've seen crypto markets actually lead equity markets over the last couple of years and crypto clearly turned down much earlier than kind of equity markets. And we've seen this high correlation to crypto and software, right? And so as crypto move lower, as software also move lower, you look at those correlations. They were pretty high. And now as, so I'm struggling a little bit with today's price action, right? Where I'm trying to understand is that the reduction or that rotation into some of the app performance of some of the software, or is there something bigger happening here? The price action is very positive if you kind of just from a technical perspective, right? Where crypto has been trying to consolidate here, we'll just take it to Bitcoin, in about a $10,000 range, low 60s to low 70s, right? And we've been consolidating while you have equity markets that are clearly breaking, right? And other asset classes that are clearly breaking to fresh lows, right? You saw Bitcoin kind of hold up in the mid 60s yesterday and we've now kind of started to bounce, right? So it's very interesting, we're watching the Clarity Act, right? There is no Clarity on Clarity right now, but you know, you saw some commentary from President Trump last week, you're kind of pushing the banks to kind of get that process moving forward. So I guess there may be some optimism on that front as well. Quickly before we go, if there's one thing we should be watching this week, what should it be? Yeah, I mean, unfortunately, it's all of the geopolitics, unfortunately, I think at this point, you know, we do have a couple of important earnings that I think people are going to pay attention to Oracle earnings, right? They're kind of very much in that AI infrastructure spending, you know, kind of paradigm right now and so, you know, they have earnings tomorrow night. And then, you know, we have a couple of pieces of economic data, PCE, the inflation side of things. Kind of at the end of this week, you know, the move higher in oil, like kind of changes a lot of different backdrops, right? In terms of, you know, just the consumer, but the interest rate, you know, kind of interest rate environment and interest rate policy going forward. So unfortunately, all things seem to come back to oil at the moment. Michael, thanks so much for joining the show and we'll see you around. Sounds good. That was Senior Market Strategist in the head of MAC Desk at the New York Stock Exchange for Michael Raking.
